page: Amazon Web Services c5n.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server instance featuring 72 vCPUs and 36 physical cores powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8124M processors running at 3.4 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the system is configured with 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding 2.67 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include any local storage or GPU hardware, meaning all storage operations rely on network-attached EBS volumes.

Performance benchmarks highlight strong multi-core capabilities and memory bandwidth. The server achieves a strong multi-core stress-ng CPU score of 67384.33 and a PassMark CPU score of 50868.09. Memory performance is notable, with read-only small block bandwidth reaching 3741.32 GB/sec and large block bandwidth at 212.97 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 25%. However, single-core performance remains average, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1193.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1458.4.

Network performance is a defining feature of this instance, offering a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps. This high-speed networking, combined with strong multi-threaded decompression capabilities and database operations, makes the instance highly cost-efficient for network-bound, compute-heavy workloads. Conversely, LLM text generation performance is poor, with only 6.09 tokens/sec on a 7B model, indicating that it is not suited for real-time generative AI inference without GPU acceleration.
Appropriate workloads for c5n.metal include high-performance computing, network appliances, intensive software compilation, and distributed database operations.
